statement0:
The word "regression" is mentioned two or more times in 11.0% of neuroscience papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "regression" , 35.4% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a higher rate than the median Psychology paper (median shown for reference); relative to other words, papers with "regression" are in the top 71st percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability.
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "regression" tend to be published in lower impact factor journals (49th percentile among all words) but tend to be cited more (51st percentile word). In general, this word is positively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are more likely to publish papers containing "regression" (63rd percentile).
